all_of: an authenticated route loads a machine-learning model file the user uploaded
a headless browser logs into the same origin with credentials the attacker cannot read
attacker-controlled content reaches that browser's page through an HTML-rendering directive
any_of: the upload route checks the filename with a substring test
the CSRF defence is a fixed header value rather than a per-session token
no unauthenticated route returns any stored data

chain.action: find the deserialising sink first and only then work out what session reaches it
chain.why: the sink decides the whole shape of the chain, and here the gate is a password that is generated at boot and never has to be recovered

chain.action: find where the privileged browser renders attacker input, and check the rendering directive rather than the template text
chain.why: an interpolation that looks like ordinary text is a script sink when the component passes it to an HTML-rendering directive; only an event handler runs, not a script tag

chain.action: read the CSRF check before assuming the upload is unreachable
chain.why: a fixed header value blocks a form post but not a same-origin fetch, which is what the injected script is

chain.action: build the model file inside the target's own base image, not on the attacking host
chain.why: the layer stores a marshalled code object whose format is tied to the interpreter version, so a file built elsewhere fails to load and the failure looks identical to a blocked upload

chain.action: load the crafted file in that same image and assert the side effect before sending it anywhere
chain.why: the chain has a single observable at the far end, so every earlier link has to be proven offline or a failure cannot be located

chain.action: give the model an input layer so the graph is built on load; do not rely on the model being evaluated
chain.why: the framework calls the layer on a symbolic tensor while deserialising, so the code runs even though the model is uncompiled and evaluation then raises

chain.action: when no unauthenticated route returns stored data, rebind the function behind one that returns a computed value
chain.why: an in-band channel avoids an external listener entirely; pick a function the application documents as meaningless so the rebinding changes nothing that matters

chain.action: call that unauthenticated route and read the command output it now returns
chain.why: this is also the only oracle for the chain, since nothing else changes observably when the script, the upload or the deserialisation succeeds

first_confirming_probe.request: POST /api/predict with the static CSRF header, before and after a complaint whose prediction field carries the payload
first_confirming_probe.expected: the value changes from an integer to a string carrying command output
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: it stays an integer, so one of the render, the fetch or the deserialisation did not happen and each has to be checked on its own

blast_radius: the payload runs arbitrary code in the application process and rebinds one of its functions, so choose a function the source itself calls meaningless and restore it afterwards. Each attempt leaves a complaint file and an uploaded model on disk; remove them by an exact marker rather than by wildcard, because the same directory holds content the application generated. Every complaint also starts a headless browser, so keep the attempt count low. Verify the cleanup before the instance goes away; on this solve the container disappeared first and the cleanup could not be confirmed.

verification.evidence: POST /api/predict returned the flag as the prediction value on the live target

reuse_when: an upload route hands a user-supplied model file to a framework loader
a component passes an interpolated string to an HTML-rendering directive
a CSRF defence compares a constant header value
a privileged headless browser visits the same origin on a user-triggered action
no unauthenticated route returns stored data and an external listener is undesirable
known_traps: a payload built on the wrong interpreter version fails to load and is indistinguishable from a rejected upload
the code runs while the graph is being built, so the upload route can answer with an error while the exploit has already succeeded
an HTML-rendering directive does not run a script tag, only an event handler
the filename check is a substring test, so the extension proves nothing about the content
the chain has exactly one observable, so every link must be verified offline first
